title: WHAT CAN I SELL?
content:
You do not need to compare every possible business idea on the internet. A much easier place to start is by deciding what kind of thing you might want a customer to pay you for.

For this library, there are four useful places to begin. You could sell something once, sell something people use up and need again, sell continuing access or value, or sell something you do for someone.

These are navigation paths, not rigid business categories. A real business can eventually combine several of them. Right now, you are only choosing which direction is worth exploring first.

WHAT THE FOUR PATHS REALLY ASK
One-Off asks whether you like a purchase that can stand on its own. Consumable asks whether you like selling something customers use up and may need again. Subscription asks whether you want to provide value that continues over time. Service asks whether the customer is paying for work performed for them.

WHAT IF MORE THAN ONE FITS?
That is normal. A coach could sell a workbook, provide coaching, recommend consumables, and run a membership. You do not need to design the whole ecosystem now. Ask which way of making your first or primary sale you want to understand next. Exploring a path is not a commitment.

QUICK CHOICE
Ask which sentence sounds most like the business you want to investigate.

"I want someone to buy a thing and have that purchase be complete." -> One-Off.
"I want to sell something people use up and need again." -> Consumable.
"I want people to keep paying because I keep providing access or value." -> Subscription.
"I want people to pay me or my business to do something for them." -> Service.

If two sound equally interesting, pick one and explore it. A branch can teach you enough to reject it, and that is still progress.

ONE-OFF
The original purchase does not inherently require another payment. Think of a guide, template, piece of furniture, course sold for one price, or another product someone can buy and own.

NEXT → PDF 03: ONE-OFF SALES

CONSUMABLE
The customer uses the product up and may need to buy it again. The important question is whether those repeat purchases also create repeat income for you.

NEXT → PDF 20: CONSUMABLE SALES

SUBSCRIPTION
The customer keeps paying because continued payment gives them continued access or value.

NEXT → PDF 31: SUBSCRIPTION SALES

SERVICE
The customer pays for something you or your business does for them.

NEXT → PDF 39: SELLING A SERVICE

You are not committing to a business by opening one of these paths. You are simply investigating it.

YOU ARE CHOOSING A STARTING POINT
If your eventual business contains several of these models, that does not make your first choice wrong. This router is answering, "Which kind of sale should I understand first?" rather than, "Which single label must describe my business forever?"

WHAT THESE FOUR OPTIONS ARE REALLY SORTING

These categories are not four mutually exclusive legal business types. They describe the basic economic promise you are considering making to a customer.

With a ONE-OFF sale, the customer pays for a complete purchase that does not inherently require another payment.

With a CONSUMABLE, the thing being purchased gets used up, creating a natural reason to buy another unit.

With a SUBSCRIPTION, continued payment preserves continued access to value.

With a SERVICE, the customer pays for work, help, expertise, or a result that you or your business performs.

A business can eventually combine them. A personal trainer might sell a one-off workout guide, recommend consumable supplements, offer monthly coaching, and run a paid membership. That does not make the categories useless. It means the trainer has several revenue models.

For now, choose the one you are trying to understand first. The goal is to find a primary direction, not design every possible revenue stream before you have a business.

HOW TO USE THE ROUTER WITHOUT OVERTHINKING IT

You are not choosing your permanent identity as a business owner.

You are choosing which question to answer next.

If two categories interest you, follow one until you understand it well enough to say yes or no. You can return here and explore the other afterward.

If your eventual business combines categories, that is fine too. What matters right now is avoiding the much harder task of trying to design several businesses at once.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Choose the path that best describes the value you want to investigate first. You can return here at any point if that path stops fitting.
